<html>
  <head>
    
  </head>
  <body>
    <p style="margin-top: 0px">
      I added a dev-server proxy block to <code>vite.config.ts</code>:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="55,186" data-copilot-content-offset="69,183" data-copilot-code-block-index="0" data-copilot-code-language="typescript"><code>server: {
  proxy: {
    '/api': {
      target: 'http://localhost:8080',
      changeOrigin: true,
    },
  },
}</code></pre>
    <p>
      What it does and why:
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>
        The React app calls the backend with a relative path (<code>fetch('/api/v1/sum?...')</code>). 
        During <code>vite dev</code>, the app is served from Vite's dev server 
        (e.g. <code>http://localhost:5173</code>), but the Go API runs on <code>http://localhost:8080</code>.
      </li>
      <li>
        Without a proxy, that cross-origin request would fail on CORS. The 
        proxy tells Vite to forward any request starting with <code>/api</code> 
        to <code>http://localhost:8080</code>, so the browser sees a 
        same-origin request and the backend receives it normally.
      </li>
      <li>
        <code>changeOrigin: true</code> rewrites the <code>Host</code> header 
        to match the target, which avoids host-based rejections on the backend 
        side.
      </li>
    </ul>
    <p>
      This only affects local development (<code>vite</code>/<code>vite dev</code>); 
      it isn't part of the production build.
    </p>
  </body>
</html>

<html>
  <head>
    
  </head>
  <body>
    <p style="margin-top: 0px">
      Done. The Go server now serves the built frontend alongside the API.
    </p>
    <h2>
      What changed
    </h2>
    <p>
      <code>server.go</code>:
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>
        Added imports <code>os</code> and <code>path/filepath</code>.
      </li>
      <li>
        Added a constant <code>frontendDistDir = &quot;frontend/dist&quot;</code> 
        (Vite's build output).
      </li>
      <li>
        Registered a catch-all route in <code>newRouter</code>: <code>mux.Handle(&quot;GET 
        /&quot;, staticFileHandler(frontendDistDir))</code>. The API patterns (<code>GET 
        /api/v1/...</code>) are more specific, so Go's <code>ServeMux</code> 
        matches them first; everything else falls through to the static 
        handler.
      </li>
      <li>
        Added <code>staticFileHandler</code>, which:

        <ul>
          <li>
            Serves real files from <code>frontend/dist</code> via <code>http.FileServer</code>.
          </li>
          <li>
            Falls back to <code>index.html</code> for the root path (<code>/</code>), 
            directories, and any missing file &#8212; the standard single-page-app 
            behavior so client routes still load the app shell.
          </li>
          <li>
            Uses <code>filepath.Clean</code>/<code>Join</code> to keep lookups 
            contained within the dist folder (guards against path traversal).
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
    <p>
      <code>main.go</code>:
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>
        Added a startup log line noting the frontend is served at <code>http://localhost:8080/</code>.
      </li>
    </ul>
    <h2>
      How to use it
    </h2>
    <p>
      Build the frontend so <code>frontend/dist</code> exists, then run the Go 
      server. Because the server's working directory needs to contain <code>frontend/dist</code>, 
      run it from the project root:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="1155,1215" data-copilot-content-offset="1169,1212" data-copilot-code-block-index="0" data-copilot-code-language="powershell"><code>cd frontend; npm run build; cd ..
go run .</code></pre>
    <p>
      Then open <code>http://localhost:8080/</code> &#8212; the Sum Calculator loads 
      and its <code>fetch('/api/v1/sum?...')</code> call hits the same origin, 
      so no proxy/CORS is needed in this mode. (The Vite dev proxy is still 
      there for <code>npm run dev</code>.)
    </p>
    <p>
      Two notes:
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>
        The static path is relative (<code>frontend/dist</code>), so the 
        server must be started from the repo root. If you'd prefer, I can make 
        it configurable via a flag or env var, or embed the assets with <code>go:embed</code> 
        so it works regardless of working directory.
      </li>
      <li>
        Unknown <code>GET</code> paths (including stray <code>/api/...</code> 
        typos) will return <code>index.html</code> by design of the SPA 
        fallback. If you'd rather return 404 for unmatched <code>/api/*</code>, 
        I can add an explicit guard.
      </li>
    </ul>
    <p>
      Want me to switch to <code>go:embed</code> so the binary is 
      self-contained?
    </p>
  </body>
</html>

      Short answer: I'm <strong>not</strong> scoping the mock to that URL &#8212; 
      the mock replaces <code>fetch</code> globally and responds the same way 
      to <em>any</em> call.
    </p>
    <p>
      Look at the test:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="153,295" data-copilot-content-offset="160,292" data-copilot-code-block-index="0" data-copilot-code-language="tsx"><code>const fetchMock = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
  ok: true,
  json: async () =&gt; ({ result: 5 }),
})
vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock)</code></pre>
    <p>
      <code>vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(...)</code> returns that same fake 
      response regardless of the arguments it's called with. So the mock isn't 
      &quot;listening&quot; for <code>/api/v1/sum</code> &#8212; it just intercepts 
      every <code>fetch</code> during the test.
    </p>
    <p>
      The URL is only verified <strong>after the fact</strong>, with this 
      assertion:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="576,648" data-copilot-content-offset="583,645" data-copilot-code-block-index="1" data-copilot-code-language="tsx"><code>expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/api/v1/sum?a=2&amp;b=3')</code></pre>
    <p>
      That checks the component actually requested the GET sum endpoint with 
      the right query string, but it doesn't drive what the mock returns.
    </p>
    <p>
      If you'd rather make the mock itself URL-aware (so a wrong URL returns a 
      rejection/404 instead of a happy result), you can switch to <code>mockImplementation</code>:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="946,1260" data-copilot-content-offset="953,1257" data-copilot-code-block-index="2" data-copilot-code-language="tsx"><code>const fetchMock = vi.fn().mockImplementation((url: string) =&gt; {
  if (url === '/api/v1/sum?a=2&amp;b=3') {
    return Promise.resolve({ ok: true, json: async () =&gt; ({ result: 5 }) })
  }
  return Promise.resolve({ ok: false, json: async () =&gt; ({ error: 'not found' }) })
})
vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock)</code></pre>

      the &quot;happy&quot;/error response when the URL exactly matches the GET sum

      response otherwise:
    </p>
    <pre data-copilot-type="code-block" data-copilot-offset="403,3107" data-copilot-content-offset="410,3104" data-copilot-code-block-index="0" data-copilot-code-language="tsx"><code>import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react'
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event'
import '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest'

import App from './App'

const SUM_URL = '/api/v1/sum?a=2&amp;b=3'

describe('App', () =&gt; {
  afterEach(() =&gt; {
    vi.restoreAllMocks()
    vi.unstubAllGlobals()
  })

  it('renders the calculator heading', () =&gt; {
    render(&lt;App /&gt;)

    expect(
      screen.getByRole('heading', { name: /sum calculator/i }),
    ).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it('shows a validation message when the numbers are missing', async () =&gt; {
    const user = userEvent.setup()
    render(&lt;App /&gt;)

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /calculate sum/i }))

    expect(screen.getByText(/please enter both numbers/i)).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it('displays the result returned for the sum of two numbers', async () =&gt; {
    const fetchMock = vi.fn().mockImplementation((url: string) =&gt; {
      if (url === SUM_URL) {
        return Promise.resolve({
          ok: true,
          json: async () =&gt; ({ result: 5 }),
        })
      }

      return Promise.resolve({
        ok: false,
        json: async () =&gt; ({ error: `unexpected request: ${url}` }),
      })
    })
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock)

    const user = userEvent.setup()
    render(&lt;App /&gt;)

    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/first number/i), '2')
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/second number/i), '3')
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /calculate sum/i }))

    await waitFor(() =&gt; {
      expect(screen.getByLabelText(/result/i)).toHaveValue('5')
    })

    expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith(SUM_URL)
  })

  it('shows the API error message when the request fails', async () =&gt; {
    const fetchMock = vi.fn().mockImplementation((url: string) =&gt; {
      if (url === SUM_URL) {
        return Promise.resolve({
          ok: false,
          json: async () =&gt; ({ error: 'invalid query parameter: b' }),
        })
      }
